prompt:
Revise the SECOND image, our current camp, with the authorised specific design corrections below. FIRST image is the original Girls' Frontline 2 rendering/colour/light reference, not a content template. Preserve the camp's current camera, room, large near-left chair and diagonally projecting armrest, side table, wide diagonal work desk, partly tucked working chair, separate tea area, rear berth, clear right aisle, two equipment cases and separate modern fireplace. Fixed scene complexity, no new furniture groups or meaningless decorative details.

DESK COMPUTER: Replace the existing small rugged terminal and its folding stand completely with ONE recognisable modern all-in-one DESKTOP COMPUTER, a moderately sized single 16:10 monitor on a slim stable stand. Position it at the existing terminal position at the far desk edge, facing and slightly turned toward the working chair; overall width is about one-third of the 1.8m desk, never a wall of displays. Graphite grey-green matte body, a dim blue-grey screen showing just a few subtle useful map/task panes, no words, logo or decorative rune. Keyboard directly in front, mouse to its right, correct seated reach and perspective. No remaining rugged tablet, radio or spare screen. Move the one open record folio and a smaller folded/partly spread map to the LEFT half of desk, with layered paper/page-edge detail and natural short shadows. Remove ALL the unidentified long rectangular slabs/boxes and the upright little block beside the lamp; keep the useful slim lamp on a simple integrated stable base. Keep working space and knee clearance. One unobtrusive power lead can follow the rear edge/desk leg, no dangling cable clutter.

UNIFY CABINET FAMILY: Tea cupboard, bed upper cabinet and bed-base drawers, and the near-right fixed equipment cabinet must share the same structural design: graphite grey-green coated frame, warm grey/stone door panels, small consistent corner radii, similar panel-frame thickness, consistent restrained joint gaps, and slender recessed pulls of the SAME cross-section. Horizontal pulls for drawers and vertical for tall doors are allowed because their use differs. Preserve subtle colour variations caused by lighting/material, no global recolour to monochrome. Remove purposeless wide black grooves, duplicate thick trim strips and miscellaneous exposed gold cabinet handles. Keep only meaningful door/drawer joints, a few actual hinges/vents/service access panels. Two portable equipment cases keep their practical clasps/handles and same physical size/colour; these are naturally different from cabinet pulls. A real entrance-door pull can remain, but must clearly belong to the entrance, not be a random ornamental cabinet accent.

REMOVE ODD DETAILS: The working-area rug stays the same shape but its dense repeated MAZE/ornamental pattern is removed. Use a quiet low-contrast woven material with subtle tonal variation, not a completely flat graphic or a crisp all-over texture. Remove the tiny meaningless patterned plaque on the column beside the fireplace, preserve the actual structural joints and necessary service panel. Jacket keeps seams/pockets/folds and no unexplained label/badge. No added props, plants, books, labels, extra screens, symbols or machinery.

Retain the calibrated source/E3 finish: nuanced round volume, rich grey-green middle colours, neutral warm-white window light and softer coloured shadow fill, selective local fine material detail rather than uniform micro-grain. Gentle atmospheric integration, task lamp/local fire subordinate, no global orange cast or flat toon blocks. Winter snow and extremely faint city outside only, no mountain/rock/castle landscape. Original postmodern city-outskirts camp about a century in the future, dry indoor room, full 16:9.
